notable_absence.finding: Unlike the sibling fts-rest-indexing/index.json's four security tiers, every one of which names a concrete internal permission string (`cluster.bucket[$BUCKET_NAME].fts!manage`/`fts!write`/`fts!read`/`stats!read`), this page's four tiers (manageCluster/readClusterSettings/readClusterLogs/writeClusterSettings) are described only in plain prose - 'permissions to manage the cluster', 'permission to read cluster settings', 'permission to read cluster logs', 'permission to write cluster settings' - with no internal permission-string literal anywhere on the page, despite the two pages sharing the same cb-swagger-generated Security section layout and the same 'Search REST APIs support HTTP basic authentication' opening sentence verbatim. The concrete-permission-string pattern this round found for index-scoped operations does not extend to node-scoped ones.

cross_component_finding: This page's RBAC gate is a different role family from every other Search Service REST endpoint checked this round: node-level configuration, diagnostics, and monitoring require the generic cluster-wide **Full Admin** or **Cluster Admin** role, with no Search-specific role (role:fts-admin/role:fts-searcher) accepted anywhere on the page - a sharp contrast with fts-rest-indexing's per-bucket Search Admin/Search Reader gate and its explicit `fts!manage`/`fts!write`/`fts!read` permission strings. The practical implication, stated nowhere on either page but derivable from the two together: a user holding Search Admin on every bucket in the cluster still cannot call any endpoint on this page - profiling a node, forcing garbage collection, or even reading a node's own runtime logs requires cluster-wide administrative privilege, not Search-service privilege. This is a real, undocumented asymmetry between the index-management and node-management halves of the same REST API family (both generated from the same cb-swagger source, per each page's own `editUrl` front matter pointing at the same GitHub repo under different `docs/modules/` paths).
cross_product_finding: Not applicable - no Capella twin exists for this page's endpoints, consistent with this round's framing for all fts-rest-* pages. No prior server/ or cloud/ extraction round names 'the planner' or 'the janitor' as Search Service internal processes, nor the known-vs-wanted node-definition distinction; these are first-contact mechanisms for the whole corpus, not just this batch.
